articles.title: The fastest double-to-string algorithm you’ve never heard of
articles.summary: The binary-to-decimal conversion library yy from ibireme uses a double-to-string algorithm to find the shortest decimal $\sigma \cdot 10^{e_{10}}$ that round-trips back to a binary float $v$ by intersecting $v$'s rounding interval with decimal grids of various spacings. This is achieved through a fixed-point approximation of $\log_{10} 2$, precomputed power-of-10 tables, and the use of only one multiplication by a precomputed power of 10 in fixed-width integer arithmetic. The library's performance is comparable to that of classic Schubfach, but with a significant reduction in computational overhead.

articles.title: A noob learns FFT
articles.summary: The Fourier transform is a powerful tool for analyzing time-frequency relationships in signals, which can be useful for tasks such as filtering, modulation analysis, and spectrum estimation. A common application of the FFT is to decompose a signal into its constituent frequencies, allowing for the identification of individual frequency components and their amplitudes. This can be particularly useful when working with noisy or complex signals that may not have clear spectral features. By analyzing the amplitude of each frequency component in the transformed signal, developers can gain insights into the underlying signal structure and make more informed decisions about data processing and analysis.
